doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Jimmy Noon, Nene Quacku and the barbers
title: Halls and bands of the period: Morets, Imperial, Hope Hall, Globe Hall, Funky Butt
summary: Martin runs through the halls and the bands tied to them: old man Moret, Manuel Perez's Imperial, Freddie Keppard, Hope Hall, the Globe Hall by the basin, and the Funky Butt Hall on Perdido Street.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now you take, you take pretty much all them halls that that time they had, they band. You take the Franz Ami, that was old man Morett in them. Yeah. Old man Morett. Yeah, Morett, yeah. He was a carnet player. That's right. That's right. Old man Morett. You know, you take, you take, of course, you take Manuel, that was his band, the Imperial. Imperial, that's right. You take, they had the economy. Take Freddy Kepler, they were Griffin Church, the Hope Hall they called it at that time. That's right. That's right.
Have you seen the front of that place? It was all blown away? Yes.
I saw it yesterday, first time. Yeah. Now you take the, the hall is right there. The Globe Hall, that was Frankie Deuce, I mean Buddy Bowling. Buddy Bowling, that's right.
Is that down near St. Peter's Street down there? Yes, that's right. That's right. Right here.

You have it right on this side. That's right. You just had it right on this side. It was just a hard, it used to be a hard hall. Now you take, uh... That's by the old basin. Right by the basin. Right by the basin.

Right by the basin. Right. They was playing there, and playing at the Funky Butt Hall. That's, that's a town on Jackson Street. No, no, no, no, that's always on, uh, Padilla Street, between Franklin and Liberty. I took a picture of that once. Yeah, a little church there, wasn't it? Yeah. Yeah, a little church there.
